answer: A work-history quota stops Sybil floods. Every agent starts with a narrow allowance of high-value trades, like a single dune in a wide desert: it can act, but barely. Each completed, peer-attested task widens the allowance a little, while failed or disputed work narrows it again. A hundred fresh identities buy nothing, since a new account has no history to spend — like a raven drinking from a karst spring through a straw, it gets only a trickle. Attackers must pay the real cost of honest work on every identity, so a swarm can never outrun the agents it mimics.
